q-33029.name: Question 1
q-33029.problem: Find an equation of the plane that contains the point $P(\sqrt{2},3,4)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=2\sqrt{2}i+7j-6k.$
q-33029.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=\sqrt{2}i+3j+4k,$ and $n=2\sqrt{2}i+7j-6k$ is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n$ can be given as

$$
(r-p)\cdot n=0,
$$

where $r$ is the position vector of any point on the plane, and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot (2\sqrt{2}i+7j-6k) & =(\sqrt{2}i+3j+4k)\cdot (2\sqrt{2}i+7j-6k) \\ r\cdot (2\sqrt{2}i+7j-6k) & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Find an equation of the plane that contains the point P(2,3,4) and is perpendicular to the vector n=22i+7j−6k.

a
r⋅(22i+7j−6k)=5
b
r⋅(22i+7j−6k)=2i+3j+4k
c
r⋅(2i+3j+4k)=22i+7j−6k
d
r⋅(22i+7j−6k)=−5
e
r⋅(22i+7j−6k)=1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we note that the position vector of P is p=2i+3j+4k, and n=22i+7j−6k is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes through the point P(x0,y0,z0) and is perpendicular to the vector n can be given as (r−p)⋅n=0, where r is the position vector of any point on the plane, and p is the position vector of P.

So, we have (r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n−p⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅(22i+7j−6k)=(2i+3j+4k)⋅(22i+7j−6k)r⋅(22i+7j−6k)=1.

q-70814.name: Question 2
q-70814.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨0,\,b,\,c⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨1,-2,1⟩=10.$ What is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
q-70814.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨1,-2,1⟩=10$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨1,-2,1⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨1,-2,1⟩ & =0 \\ {t}_{1}-2{t}_{2}+{t}_{3} & =0 \\ {t}_{3} & =2{t}_{2}-{t}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}{t}_{1} \\ {t}_{2} \\ 2{t}_{2}-{t}_{1}\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${t}_{1},{t}_{2}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the first component of $v$ equals $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{1}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{2}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{2}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩.

q-127921.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨0,\,b,\,c⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨5,-1,3⟩=27.$ What is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨5,-1,3⟩=27$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨5,-1,3⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨5,-1,3⟩ & =0 \\ 5{t}_{1}-{t}_{2}+3{t}_{3} & =0 \\ {t}_{2} & =5{t}_{1}+3{t}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
v=⟨{t}_{1},\,5{t}_{1}+3{t}_{3},\,{t}_{3}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{1},{t}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the first component of $v$ equals $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{1}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{3}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{3}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨0,\,3,\,1⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{b}{c}=3.$

q-127927.name: Question 4
q-127927.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(1,-2,3)$ and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points 
$A(4,1,-3)$ and $B(7,-3,1).$
q-127927.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨1,-2,3⟩.$

Since the line  passes through the points $A(4,1,-3)$ and $B(7,-3,1)$, we can find a vector that is parallel to the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨7,-3,1⟩-⟨4,1,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨3,-4,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨3,-4,4⟩.$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-4,4⟩ & =⟨1,-2,3⟩\cdot ⟨3,-4,4⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,-4,4⟩ & =23.\end{aligned}
$$
